primary_claim: LLMs (GPT-J, Pythia-6.9B, Llama3.1-8B) represent integers as a helix combining periodic Fourier features (periods 2, 5, 10, 100) with a linear component, and compute a+b by manipulating the helices for a and b via a Clock-algorithm-like mechanism, mostly implemented in MLPs 14-27 of GPT-J.

effect.metric: task accuracy on a+b for a,b in [0,99] (GPT-J)
effect.value: 80% of prompts successfully completed; ablating the fitted helix dimensions affects performance roughly as much as ablating the full residual stream h_a^l

contradicts_or_qualifies: Finds evidence against the strongest form of the Linear Representation Hypothesis, similar to Engels et al., since numbers are represented as a multidimensional helical manifold rather than a purely linear direction
limitations_stated: Do not know the exact low-level mechanism used to construct helix(a+b) from helix(a,b), though hypothesize trigonometric angle-addition identities
Results for Llama3.1-8B are weaker than for GPT-J and Pythia-6.9B, with helix(a+b) a considerably worse fit on last-token hidden states
Study focused on models with single-token representations of two-digit numbers; models with single-digit tokenization (e.g. Gemma-2-9B) likely require additional algorithms
quote: We find that three mid-sized LLMs represent numbers as helices and manipulate them using the interpretable Clock algorithm to compute addition.
